display.title: The Baal Shem Tov and the Lambskin
display.summary_short: A poor innkeeper who owes the poritz two years' rent goes to the Baal Shem Tov, who sends him to buy a plain lambskin and give it to the poritz as a birthday gift.
display.summary_long: Moshe, a pious innkeeper, rents his inn from a poritz. The old poritz was patient, but his son, a big spender, is harsh, and after two bad years Moshe owes two years' rent. The poritz has him beaten and threatens to throw the whole family into prison. Moshe's wife reminds him to trust in Hashem and urges him to visit the Baal Shem Tov in Mezhibuzh. Though doubtful, Moshe goes, and the Baal Shem Tov gives him a silver coin: buy the first thing a peasant offers you at the market and bring it to me. It is a small lambskin, and the Baal Shem Tov calls it remarkable and tells Moshe to give it to the poritz at his birthday party. Ashamed among the nobles' costly gifts, Moshe brings it anyway, and the poritz, embarrassed, has him locked in the cellar. Then a guest spreads out the skin and finds the poritz's name, birthday and family emblem woven into it like a work of art. The delighted poritz forgives the debt, gives Moshe the inn rent-free forever and sends him home with gold and silver. The storyteller closes with a call to give tzedakah and ask for Moshiach.
display.lesson: Trust in Hashem and follow a tzaddik's advice, even when it makes no sense to you.

date.note: Closing: 'say we want Moshiach now, so we have a real Hakhel'; suggests 5776 or 5783.

advisories.note: The poritz has the innkeeper beaten and later locked in a cellar.
A poor family is threatened with prison and losing their home over unpaid rent.
